review_text:
Para mí, Among Us es mucho más que un juego para pasar el rato. Aunque parece un juego simple en el que solo tenés que descubrir quién es el impostor, creo que también puede enseñarnos bastante sobre nosotros mismos y sobre cómo nos relacionamos con los demás.

Una de las cosas que más me gusta es el tema de la confianza. En el juego tenés que confiar en otras personas, pero también tenés que aprender a pensar por vos mismo. A veces confiás en alguien y resulta que te estaba mintiendo, y otras veces sospechás de alguien que no tenía nada que ver. Eso te enseña que no siempre las primeras impresiones son correctas y que está bien equivocarse.

También creo que ayuda a mejorar la forma en la que nos comunicamos. Tenemos que escuchar a los demás, explicar lo que vimos, defender nuestras ideas y, sobre todo, aceptar cuando podemos estar equivocados. Aprender a decir “me equivoqué” es algo importante, no solo en un juego, sino también en la vida.

Además, jugar con otras personas puede enseñarnos a tener más paciencia y empatía. Cada persona piensa de una manera diferente y toma decisiones distintas. En vez de enojarnos porque alguien no piensa como nosotros, podemos intentar entender por qué llegó a esa conclusión.

Por eso siento que Among Us puede dejar algo positivo. No porque necesariamente nos haga mejores personas por jugarlo, sino porque las situaciones que vivimos dentro del juego pueden hacernos reflexionar sobre cómo somos nosotros mismos. Nos permite aprender a confiar, a cuestionar nuestras propias ideas, a escuchar a los demás y a aceptar nuestros errores.

Al final, ganar una partida está bueno, pero también está bueno terminar una partida habiendo aprendido algo sobre nosotros mismos. Y creo que eso es lo más interesante de Among Us: que, detrás de descubrir quién es el impostor, también podemos descubrir un poco más sobre nosotros mismos.

ATT:  Un fan de Among Us.
translated_text:
For me, Among Us is much more than just a game to pass the time. Although it seems like a simple game where you just have to figure out who the imposter is, I think it can also teach us a lot about ourselves and how we relate to others.

One of the things I like most is the theme of trust. In the game, you have to trust other people, but you also have to learn to think for yourself. Sometimes you trust someone and it turns out they were lying to you, and other times you suspect someone who had nothing to do with it. That teaches you that first impressions aren't always correct and that it's okay to be wrong.

I also think it helps improve the way we communicate. We have to listen to others, explain what we saw, defend our ideas, and, above all, accept when we might be wrong. Learning to say "I was wrong" is important, not only in a game but also in life.

Furthermore, playing with other people can teach us to be more patient and empathetic. Everyone thinks differently and makes different decisions. Instead of getting angry because someone doesn't think like us, we can try to understand why they reached that conclusion.

That's why I feel that Among Us can offer something positive. Not because it necessarily makes us better people by playing it, but because the situations we experience within the game can make us reflect on who we are. It allows us to learn to trust, to question our own ideas, to listen to others, and to accept our mistakes.

In the end, winning a game is great, but it's also great to finish a game having learned something about ourselves. And I think that's the most interesting thing about Among Us: that, beyond discovering who the imposter is, we can also discover a little more about ourselves.

review_text:
Lethal Company é um jogo sobre um emprego totalmente normal, no qual seu empregador o envia para luas abandonadas cheias de monstros aterrorizantes e depois fica irritado se você não trouxer sucata suficiente.

Basicamente, é como trabalhar num depósito da Amazon, mas, de alguma forma, pior.

A premissa é simples.

Você pousa em uma lua.

Você entra em um prédio.

Você coleta sucata.

Você a leva de volta para a nave.

Você bate a meta.

Fácil.

Só que o prédio é basicamente um labirinto assombrado gigante, as luzes mal funcionam e existem cerca de 400 maneiras diferentes de você e seus amigos morrerem.

E seu empregador não está nem aí.

Você pode ser devorado por um monstro.

Você pode cair em um buraco.

Você pode ser esmagado.

Você pode se perder.

Você pode ver seu melhor amigo sendo arrastado para a escuridão.

A Companhia não se importa.

Bata a meta.

É só isso.

O jogo fica melhor quando jogado com amigos, porque Lethal Company, de alguma forma, transforma o terror de sobrevivência básico no desastre de trabalho mais engraçado possível.

Uma pessoa está explorando.

Alguém está carregando sucata.

Alguém está monitorando as telas.

Alguém está do lado de fora esperando por todos.

E sempre tem aquela pessoa que diz:

“Pessoal, achei uma coisa.”

Você sabe imediatamente que isso vai acabar mal.

Eles entram mais fundo.

Você ouve gritos.

“Você está bem?”

“Não.”

“Onde você está?”

“Não sei.”

“O que está te perseguindo?”

“EU NÃO SEI.”

Então, o microfone deles fica mudo.

Você olha para o monitor.

Eles sumiram.

Bom.

Pelo menos conseguimos a sucata.

Os monstros também são fantásticos, porque você nunca sabe realmente o que vai encontrar.

Alguns inimigos podem ser evitados.

Alguns podem ser distraídos.

Alguns exigem trabalho em equipe.

Alguns existem basicamente para arruinar o seu dia inteiro.

E o pior é que seus amigos costumam ser mais perigosos do que os monstros.

Alguém deixa uma porta aberta. Alguém apaga as luzes.

Alguém pega a única lanterna.

Alguém se perde.

Alguém pega um objeto que não deveria tocar de jeito nenhum.

Alguém diz: "Acho que estamos seguros."

Cinco segundos depois, você está morto.

O chat de voz por proximidade torna tudo ainda melhor.

Você ouve seus amigos se afastando.

A voz deles vai ficando mais baixa.

Então você ouve:

"PESSOAL?"

Você corre em direção a eles.

"PESSOAL, ACHO QUE TEM ALGUMA COISA AQUI."

Você chega lá.

Eles sumiram.

Você ouve a voz deles vindo de longe:

"CORRE."

Você corre.

Não faz perguntas.

Você simplesmente corre.

E há também os momentos em que o jogo é genuinamente aterrorizante.

Você está sozinho.

A bateria da sua lanterna está acabando.

Você não vê nada há vários minutos.

Você está carregando uma sucata valiosa.

Você ouve passos atrás de você.

Você se vira.

Nada.

Você continua andando.

Outro barulho.

Agora você se move mais rápido.

Você chega à entrada.

Você acha que está seguro.

Algo ataca você.

Você grita.

Seu amigo está rindo no microfone.

É isso que Lethal Company faz de melhor.

O jogo cria um terror genuíno e, logo em seguida, o estraga com seus amigos agindo como idiotas.

O sistema de sucata também torna tudo mais estressante do que deveria ser.

Normalmente, se você encontrasse algo valioso em um jogo de terror, ficaria empolgado.

Em Lethal Company, você morre de medo de perder o item.

Você passou vinte minutos coletando sucata.

Seu inventário está cheio.

Você está quase de volta à nave.

Você praticamente sente o gosto do dinheiro.

Então, algo mata você.

Toda a sua sucata fica caída no chão.

Seus amigos ainda estão vivos.

Eles têm uma única missão:

Pegar a sucata.

Eles não pegam.

Eles vão embora.

Você os vê voltando para a órbita sem absolutamente nada.

Agora, você tem mais medo dos seus amigos do que dos monstros.

E, de alguma forma, isso ainda não é suficiente para impedir que você jogue novamente.

Porque cada partida cria uma história.

Você não se lembra das expedições comuns.

Você se lembra do desastre.

Da vez em que alguém ficou preso atrás de uma porta.

Da vez em que seu amigo foi morto cinco segundos depois de dizer: "Acho que estamos seguros".

Da vez em que alguém carregou uma quantidade absurda de sucata de volta para a nave.

Da vez em que todos morreram e uma pessoa sobreviveu, de alguma forma, escondida num canto por vinte minutos.

Da vez em que você bateu a meta por uma margem mínima.

Da vez em que você não atingiu a meta por apenas um dólar.

Da vez em que todos riam tanto que ninguém percebeu o monstro caminhando em sua direção.

Lethal Company é o exemplo perfeito de um jogo com mecânicas simples, mas que gera situações infinitamente divertidas.

Você não é um herói.

Você não está salvando o mundo.

Você não está lutando pela humanidade.

Você é um funcionário.

Seu chefe quer sucata.

Pegue a sucata.

Tente não morrer.

E, se você morrer, tomara que seus amigos se lembrem de trazer seu corpo de volta.

10/10. Arriscaria minha vida por um salário mínimo novamente.
translated_text:
Lethal Company is a game about a totally normal job where your employer sends you to abandoned moons full of terrifying monsters and then gets angry if you don't bring back enough scrap.

Basically, it's like working in an Amazon warehouse, but somehow worse.

The premise is simple.

You land on a moon.

You enter a building.

You collect scrap.

You take it back to the ship.

You meet the goal.

Easy.

Except the building is basically a giant haunted maze, the lights barely work, and there are about 400 different ways you and your friends can die.

And your employer doesn't care.

You can be devoured by a monster.

You can fall into a hole.

You can be crushed.

You can get lost.

You can watch your best friend being dragged into the darkness.

The Company doesn't care.

Meet the goal. That's all.

The game is better when played with friends because Lethal Company somehow transforms basic survival horror into the funniest possible workplace disaster.

One person is exploring.

Someone is carrying scrap.

Someone is monitoring the screens.

Someone is outside waiting for everyone.

And there's always that one person who says:

“Guys, I found something.”

You know immediately this is going to end badly.

They go deeper.

You hear screams.

“Are you okay?”

“No.”

“Where are you?”

“I don’t know.”

“What’s chasing you?”

“I DON’T KNOW.”

Then their microphone goes silent.

You look at the monitor.

They’ve disappeared.

Good.

At least we got the scrap.

The monsters are fantastic too, because you never really know what you're going to find.

Some enemies can be avoided.

Some can be distracted.

Some require teamwork.

Some exist basically to ruin your entire day.

And the worst part is that your friends are often more dangerous than the monsters.

Someone leaves a door open. Someone turns off the lights.

Someone grabs the only flashlight.

Someone gets lost.

Someone picks up an object they shouldn't touch at all.

Someone says, "I think we're safe."

Five seconds later, you're dead.

Near-field voice chat makes it even better.

You hear your friends walking away.

Their voices get quieter.

Then you hear:

"GUYS?"

You run towards them.

"GUYS, I THINK THERE'S SOMETHING HERE."

You get there.

They disappeared.

You hear their voices coming from afar:

"RUN."

You run.

You don't ask questions.

You simply run.

And then there are the moments when the game is genuinely terrifying.

You're alone.

Your flashlight battery is dying.

You haven't seen anything for several minutes.

You're carrying valuable scrap metal.

You hear footsteps behind you.

You turn around.

Nothing.

You keep walking.

Another noise.

Now you move faster.

You reach the entrance.

You think you're safe.

Something attacks you.

You scream.

Your friend is laughing into the microphone.

That's what Lethal Company does best.

The game creates genuine terror and then ruins it with your friends acting like idiots.

The scrap system also makes everything more stressful than it should be.

Normally, if you found something valuable in a horror game, you'd be thrilled.

In Lethal Company, you're terrified of losing the item.

You've spent twenty minutes collecting scrap.

Your inventory is full.

You're almost back on the ship.

You can practically taste the money.

Then, something kills you.

All your scrap is scattered on the floor.

Your friends are still alive.

They have a single mission:

To retrieve the scrap.

They don't.

They leave.

You watch them return to orbit with absolutely nothing.

Now, you're more afraid of your friends than the monsters.

And somehow, that's still not enough to stop you from playing again.

Because each playthrough creates a story.

You don't remember the usual expeditions.

Do you remember the disaster?

The time someone got trapped behind a door.

The time your friend was killed five seconds after saying, "I think we're safe."

The time someone carried an absurd amount of scrap metal back to the ship.

The time everyone died and one person somehow survived, hiding in a corner for twenty minutes.

The time you narrowly missed the goal.

The time you missed the goal by just one dollar.

The time everyone was laughing so hard that nobody noticed the monster walking towards them.

Lethal Company is the perfect example of a game with simple mechanics, but which generates endlessly fun situations.

You're not a hero.

You're not saving the world.

You're not fighting for humanity.

You're an employee.

Your boss wants scrap metal.

Get the scrap metal.

Try not to die.

And if you die, hopefully your friends will remember to bring your body back.

10/10. I would risk my life for minimum wage again.

Le jeu est sympa et le concept est vraiment cool, surtout entre amis, mais honnêtement je trouve qu'il devient vite chiant à cause des mobs.

On peut se faire tuer en 2 secondes, parfois sans avoir vraiment le temps de comprendre ce qui nous arrive. Le pire, c'est qu'on a souvent absolument aucun moyen de se défendre. Tu croises un mob, il t'attaque, et c'est quasiment fini. Tu peux courir, essayer de comprendre ce qu'il faut faire, mais dans beaucoup de situations tu ne peux simplement rien faire à part regarder ton personnage mourir. Je trouve ça vraiment frustrant, surtout quand tu viens à peine de commencer une partie. Tu peux passer plusieurs minutes à explorer pour finalement te faire tuer en quelques secondes par un mob contre lequel tu ne pouvais quasiment rien faire. Et une fois mort, tu dois juste attendre que tes potes finissent leur partie. Donc au final, tu passes parfois plus de temps à attendre qu'à jouer, ce qui me fait vraiment décrocher du jeu. C'est dommage parce que le concept est vraiment sympa et il y a clairement du potentiel. J'aimerais juste que les mobs soient moins punitifs ou qu'on ait davantage de moyens de réagir et de se défendre. Le manque de nouveau contenu est aussi dommage, mais pour moi le vrai problème reste clairement les mobs et le fait de pouvoir mourir beaucoup trop facilement.
translated_text:
The game is fun and the concept is really cool, especially with friends, but honestly, I find it gets boring quickly because of the mobs.

You can get killed in two seconds, sometimes without even having time to understand what's happening. The worst part is that you often have absolutely no way to defend yourself. You come across a mob, it attacks you, and that's pretty much it. You can run, try to figure out what to do, but in many situations, there's simply nothing you can do except watch your character die. I find that really frustrating, especially when you've just started a game. You can spend several minutes exploring only to get killed in seconds by a mob you could barely do anything about. And once you're dead, you just have to wait for your friends to finish their game. So, in the end, you sometimes spend more time waiting than playing, which really makes me lose interest. It's a shame because the concept is really fun and there's clearly potential. I just wish the mobs were less punishing or that we had more ways to react and defend ourselves. The lack of new content is also a shame, but for me the real problem is clearly the mobs and the fact that you can die far too easily.

review_text:
★★★★★

Absolutely chaotic and way more fun than it has any right to be.

Content Warning is one of those games that becomes 10x better when you're playing with friends. The whole idea of going into creepy locations, recording terrifying things, and trying to make it back alive with enough footage is such a simple concept, but it creates so many hilarious situations.

The biggest selling point for me is the multiplayer experience. You can have a completely normal plan going into a mission, and within about two minutes everyone is running around screaming, getting separated, forgetting what they're supposed to be doing, and leaving someone behind.

The video-recording mechanic is also a really cool idea. You're actually encouraged to get close to the creepy stuff because you need footage, which makes the usual horror-game instinct of "GET AWAY FROM THAT" conflict with "WAIT, I NEED TO RECORD THIS."

The environments are creepy, the monsters are unsettling, and the limited visibility makes exploring genuinely tense. You never quite know what you're going to run into.

But honestly, half the fun isn't even the horror. It's watching your friends completely lose their minds when something appears behind them while you're trying to warn them.

There's also a great risk/reward feeling to the game. You want to explore further and get better footage, but the longer you stay, the more likely things are to go horribly wrong.

It's not a massive, complicated game, but it doesn't need to be. It's designed around creating memorable multiplayer moments, and it absolutely succeeds at that.

If you've got a group of friends who enjoy horror games and don't mind a bit of absolute stupidity, I'd definitely recommend it.

9/10 — terrifying, hilarious, chaotic, and an absolute blast with friends.

A very relaxing and entertaining game. I mostly prefer to fish alone as I get to focus on slowly completing the collection but from my public experience, most of the players seemed normal and very eager to converse about very different topics. There will always be few bad apples here and there but majority of players even now are nice. The gameplay is of course simple and repetitive but I like these types of games. Cosmetics (including labels) are cute and easily obtainable, fishing mechanics aren't difficult either. I have not fully completed everything, as it takes times to later upgrade your rod but some lures seemed almost useless so you can avoid those (my preferences were to go for a lucky hook (every dollar counts in early game) and then jump straight for the attractive lure as other lures were... just aight.) NOT saying you cannot buy em, the double hook was also useful but a lot of those are only use for VERY specific parts of the collection (like collecting all rarities of trash). 

The fishing buddy is easy to upgrade and set-up, good passive income though not much to expect from rarity even when upgraded, it's not crazy profits. I only for now have the freshwater bucket because I rarely fish in the saltwater (will be forced to change that for the collection fair fair). I barely use the aquarium but might try to impress some shawty (jk jk) with a fish anyone can catch if they just continue playing the game-

This game was on my wishlist for a whileeee, I kept thinking "oh yeah I will just wait for the sale" (as I always felt off buying something at full price) but really??? the game never had a sale and probably never will, it's just 5 euros  and if you love fishing, this IS the game xd. I never wanted to shame the developer for not giving this game a sale (In fact, I hope they are doing alright, I didn't know before what happened to the game for not getting any active updates but even then, I think the game in its abandoned state is fine enough to play), I am just explaining the reason why it stayed unbought for so long lol. (it's shown as gifted because my brother asks to buy me the game through steam and I pay him irl, I know this looks weird about me talking about the price when the star shows as if I didn't buy it XD)

Sounds are nice but I prefer to turn on my own random playlists I have, if you try switching tabs, chat while waiting for you catch, if it's raining in-game, it can be harder to hear anything but otherwise that's doable when the skies are clear. 

Overall, fun, simple and effective in what it presents and gives. Pretty calm community, can be played alone just fine. Cute ways to customise your lil buddy and neat emotes. OH YEAH- cute artstyle, gives me a nostalgic feeling of older games with these simpler graphics, very lovely.

マルチプレイで楽しめるまったりした雰囲気の釣りゲー、
日本語は現時点で非対応。英語のみ。

色々な釣り具と魚たちが存在し、張り付いてみっちり釣ってもいいし、ある程度放置してときどきチェックするような遊び方もOK。
キャラクターのスキンが豊富だったりやけに凝った楽器演奏が出来たりと、釣り以外の要素も充実している側面がある。
できれば日本人の友達とマルチで遊んでみたいが、今のところやってくれる知り合いがいないｗ
たとえばマビノギで釣り堀に行ってギルドチャットしながら釣りをしているときみたいな、あの雰囲気になりそう。（演奏もできるし）
そのうえで、このゲームにはこのゲームならではの独特の雰囲気があるので、完全にマビノギと一緒にはならないだろう。

今後もゆっくり時間をかけてクエストボードのミッションを進めていきたい。

[h1]A unique atmosphere that's addictive[/h1]

A laid-back fishing game that can be enjoyed in multiplayer.
Japanese is not currently supported. English only.

There are various fishing tools and fish, and you can either stick to it and fish diligently, or play by leaving it idle for a while and checking occasionally.
It also has elements other than fishing, such as a wide variety of character skins and surprisingly elaborate musical instrument performance.
I'd like to play multiplayer with Japanese friends if possible, but I don't know anyone who would play with me at the moment lol
It seems like it would have the same atmosphere as when you go to a fishing pond in Mabinogi and fish while chatting with your guild. (You can also play musical instruments.)
Furthermore, this game has its own unique atmosphere, so it won't be exactly the same as Mabinogi.

I want to continue slowly progressing through the quest board missions.

Phasmophobia é um jogo de investigação paranormal onde você entra em uma casa para descobrir qual fantasma está ali..

“EMF, temperatura, Spirit Box, câmera, livro… hoje eu vou trabalhar direito.”
O fantasma:

apaga a luz
abre uma porta
joga uma coisa no chão
anda pela casa inteira
não dá evidência nenhuma

Você: “beleza 👍”

Até o fantasma começar a fazer coisas que te fazem questionar todas as suas decisões de vida.

…e o jogo te mostra que você estava errado.

Os bugs e comportamentos estranhos só completam a experiência.
E mesmo assim?
“Mais uma partida.”

Porque aparentemente meu instinto de sobrevivência desaparece completamente quando existe a possibilidade de ganhar dinheiro identificando corretamente uma entidade sobrenatural.

Jogo excelente. Assustador, engraçado, caótico e ocasionalmente tão absurdo que o verdadeiro fantasma parece ser o próprio código.

Recomendo. Principalmente se você gosta de sofrer com amigos.
translated_text:
Phasmophobia is a paranormal investigation game where you enter a house to discover which ghost is inside.

You arrive with your equipment, all professional:

“EMF, temperature, Spirit Box, camera, book… today I’m going to do this properly.”

The ghost:

turns off the light
opens a door
throws something on the floor
walks around the whole house
gives no evidence whatsoever

You: “Great 👍”

Then finally some evidence appears and you start putting together the investigation like a rational person.

Until the ghost starts doing things that make you question all your life decisions.

And then there’s that wonderful moment when you’re 100% convinced you know which ghost it is, you mark the answer, take the exit…

…and the game shows you that you were wrong.

There are also matches where the ghost seems to have specifically chosen your equipment as a personal enemy. Camera being thrown, doors moving, objects flying, and you trying to figure out if you’re investigating a ghost or participating in a condo dispute.

The bugs and strange behaviors only complete the experience.

And even then?

“One more game.”

Because apparently my survival instinct completely disappears when there's a possibility of making money by correctly identifying a supernatural entity.

Excellent game. Scary, funny, chaotic, and occasionally so absurd that the real ghost seems to be the code itself.

I recommend it. Especially if you like suffering with friends.

review_text:
I have mixed feelings about the recent Phasmophobia updates. Unfortunately, I keep getting matched with extremely toxic players. I can't tell if it's the community or just bad luck, but in my experience it's safest not to talk in lobbies unless someone speaks to you first, because it often ends with a racial slur being thrown at me or one of my friends and it's repulsive. This happens in nearly every other match, and I shouldn't have to put up with it. One bad game wouldn't bother me, but the frequency wore me down. Phasmophobia is a game about hunting ghosts, and I wish the conversation would stay there.

What bothers me most is how many people in this community seem to think racism is funny. Racism is never funny, in any context, and if you think it is, you are part of the problem. It points to a bigger underlying issue, and I don't understand how it has gone unaddressed for so long. Popular creators rarely speak up about it, and the behavior is seldom called out by players or the people running the game, so it just keeps going.

Optimization also seems to be getting worse with each update. To be clear, the game runs great on my newer rig, at over 420 FPS, so if you have a newer card you're fine, it feels about as light as running a browser on the side it's that smooth. On my older system, though, it struggled badly, even though I've seen players with weaker rigs holding a steady 30 FPS. I couldn't manage that, so between the performance and the matchmaking, I uninstalled. SO I wouldn't suggest buying or playing this game with something like a GTX 1650 which is the bare minimum atleast these days if not a 2080 Super so optimization still is horrible. Not everybody can upgrade every generation.

What I wish for most is a game that feels cooperative. A co-op game should make people want to work together, and that starts with being welcoming to newer players. Phasmophobia has a steep learning curve, and plenty of people don't have time to study ghost types and evidence on top of school, work, or a college degree they're trying to finish. New players shouldn't be pushed out or made to feel stupid for not knowing everything yet. If the community focused on teaching and encouraging each other instead of tearing each other down, this could be a great game. As it stands, I can't recommend a co-op game that so rarely feels cooperative.

That said, I have had, and still occasionally have, good times in this game. I've met great people who also try to avoid those kinds of lobbies, and some of them have resorted to hosting their own private or public lobbies just so they can control who stays and kick the toxic players, because they don't want to deal with that. I still believe the game has real potential as something to play with your own friends. If you're going to pick a co-op game, this is a much better choice for your friend group than most of the throwaway party or "slop" games out there, and that's always a great idea. Otherwise, I really struggle to love the current state of the community and the recent updates, especially the changes to the maps.

review_text:
Fun premise, decently well executed. There's a few complaints here and there (clashing artstyles, gameplay loop quickly turns stale) but I think my biggest complaint would be ranking system when you're back at HQ.

To compare it to Content Warning: CW's video ranking system glues together a funny video at least half of the time. The screaming, abrupt cuts, funny ragdolling: Headliners really misses that moment of coming back to the base and laughing at what you've captured. In my experience, we've chuckled a few times at some silly photo, but unfortunately the game conditions you too much into taking good photos, not funny ones.

And thus, you come back to the base and the top 5 photos are usually just a compilation of monsters and chaos, the player capturing as much as they can in one frame. There will be something funny sometimes, but by pure accident. In that regard, Headliners is a bit of a letdown. Otherwise it's a fun game to play with friends.

review_text:
Escape the Backrooms is a great game for exploring a place that looks like it was designed by someone who heard the word “office” and decided to make it everyone’s problem. The empty rooms, endless corridors, and strange spaces create a creepy atmosphere that makes you want to keep moving—even when you have absolutely no idea where you’re going.

Playing with friends makes the experience more fun, partly because you can work together and partly because being lost is much better when several people are confidently lost at the same time. One person says, “I think it’s this way,” and the rest of the group follows them with the trust normally reserved for a qualified tour guide. Then you all end up in another suspicious hallway.

There’s a good mix of exploring, figuring out what to do, and trying to avoid the things you’d rather not meet. It can be tense, but it can also be very funny when everyone panics at once. Would recommend if you like co-op horror and don’t mind spending a surprising amount of time asking, “Have we been here already?

review_text: This game is great, though i have a couple suggestions. A: Anti-camping feature. There's a lot of players who will just place a Specialist in a Wuggy hatch and just sit there and wait until someone triggers something that tells them where a Specialist is or until someone comes to save them, at which point they kill the other player and stuff them in a Wuggy hatch too. It'd be hard to come up with a lore reason, but it'd be easy to add an if statement to say if the monster is too close, the death timer won't go down or something else. B: Further Low-end compatibility. This game runs well on a low end device, but i frequently see what is either a matchmaking bug or my computer being funky when the game takes place anywhere but the theatre it just won't work and in the corner menu during matchmaking,  sometimes it'll go to a negative number. C: An in depth tutorial. Maybe it's more computer issues, but I never found a tutorial, which frustrated me when i had to learn the controls while being hunted by Boxy Boo. (or hunting as mommy long legs) Trying to hide in a port-a-lounge as they approached failed when i used my grab pack to do it (I assumed that it used the grab pack because everything else did, from closing doors to saving teammates, to puzzles.)And if you couldn't tell I got attacked. Don't get me wrong. I still appreciate this game, and i'd still play it as is, but these would just make the player experience better, at least in my view. Love the gameplay (and the option for third person, because again, not a horror guy) and the setting and lore are pretty good. Thanks for making this, Mob. (P.S. This was actually my entry into the world of horror games. If this counts as such.)

review_text:
Genel Değerlendirme:
Deceit 2, masum oyuncuların arasına sızmış kana susamış enfekte (Canavar) oyuncuların kimliğini ortaya çıkarmaya dayalı birinci şahıs nişancı ve sosyal çıkarım unsurlarını harmanlayan gerilim dolu bir korku oyunu. Oyuncular bir yandan haritada koşturup ritüelleri tamamlamaya ve hayatta kalma ekipmanları bulmaya çalışırken, diğer yandan "Kim gerçek, kim hain?" paranoyasıyla birbirlerini süzmek zorunda kalıyor. Görsel atmosferin karanlığı, ses tasarımı ve oylama mekanizmaları oyun boyunca tansiyonu hiç düşürmeyen bir hayatta kalma mücadelesi sunuyor.

Artıları:

Yüksek Gerilim ve Paranoya Atmosferi: Oyuncuların iki farklı boyuta (gerçek dünya ve kan ritüeli dünyası) geçebilmesi, kimin ne zaman dönüşeceğini bilememenin yarattığı o sürekli tedirginlik hissini tavan yaptırıyor.

Arkadaş Gruplarıyla Oynandığında Tavana Vuran Eğlence: Discord veya sesli sohbet üzerinden "Kesinlikle o enfekte, ben gözlerimle gördüm!" şeklindeki suçlamalar ve iftiralarla dolu hararetli tartışmalar unutulmaz anlar yaşatıyor.

Rol Çeşitliliği ve Stratejik Derinlik: Sadece masum ve canavar ayrımı değil; masumları manipüle eden lanetli roller ve dedektiflik mekanikleri oyuna ekstra bir taktiksel katman ekliyor.

Yenilenen Görsel Kalite: İlk oyuna kıyasla çok daha modern grafiklere, detaylı haritalara ve korku ögelerini pekiştiren kaliteli bir ses tasarımına sahip.

Eksileri:

Rastgele (Public) Eşleşmelerdeki İletişim Eksikliği: Mikrofon kullanmayan, oyunu terk eden veya haksız yere oy veren rastgele oyuncularla eşleştiğinizde oyunun tüm atmosferi ve mantığı maalesef zedelenebiliyor.

Öğrenme Eğrisi: Yeni başlayanlar için harita mekaniklerini, ritüel eşyalarını ve suçlama dengesini oturtmak ilk başta biraz kafa karıştırıcı ve zor olabiliyor.

Sonuç:
Among Us tarzı sosyal aldatma mekaniklerini birinci şahıs korku atmosferiyle birleştiren, arkadaş grubunuzla çığlıklar atarak oynayacağınız son derece heyecan verici ve gerilim dolu bir yapım.

Puan: 7.5/10
translated_text:
Overall Assessment:
Deceit 2 is a tense horror game that blends first-person shooter and social deduction elements, focusing on uncovering the identities of bloodthirsty infected (Monster) players who have infiltrated the ranks of innocent players. Players must simultaneously scrutinize each other with paranoia, wondering "Who is real, who is a traitor?" as they race across the map, completing rituals and finding survival gear. The dark visual atmosphere, sound design, and voting mechanisms create a survival struggle that maintains constant tension throughout the game.

Pros:

High Tension and Paranoia Atmosphere: The ability for players to switch between two different dimensions (the real world and the world of blood rituals) heightens the constant anxiety of not knowing who will transform when.

Enhanced Fun When Played with Friends: Heated discussions filled with accusations and slanders like "That's definitely the infected one, I saw it with my own eyes!" via Discord or voice chat create unforgettable moments.

Role Variety and Strategic Depth: It's not just about distinguishing between innocent and monster; cursed roles manipulating the innocent and detective mechanics add an extra tactical layer to the game.

Renewed Visual Quality: Compared to the first game, it boasts much more modern graphics, detailed maps, and high-quality sound design that enhances the horror elements.

Cons:

Lack of Communication in Random (Public) Matchmaking: When matched with random players who don't use microphones, leave the game, or vote unfairly, the entire atmosphere and logic of the game can unfortunately be damaged.

Learning Curve: For beginners, understanding the map mechanics, ritual items, and blame balance can be a bit confusing and difficult at first.

Conclusion:

A highly exciting and suspenseful game that combines Among Us-style social deception mechanics with a first-person horror atmosphere, perfect for playing with your group of friends while screaming.

Score: 7.5/10

Я являюсь преданным фанатом Deceit 1 и не последнего билда, а версии Legacy. Наиграл там около трёхсот часов и застал, по моему мнению, золотое время для этой игрушки — 2020 год.

Сейчас я не могу поиграть в этот режим, потому что разрабы отключили сервера. Да, в последний билд первой части ещё оставили возможность зайти, но в легаси режим не подключается. Ну что же, решили попробовать вторую часть, на которую нас так вынуждали перейти разработчики.

Что могу сказать? Из явных плюсов это графон. Ну, лично я кайфанул от визуальной картинки. Но геймплей... Да, вроде больше ролей, больше возможностей, но в итоге ты и половину не успеваешь применить. Нужно выполнить стопятьсот заданий, ещё следить при этом за алтарями и вычислять заражённых, среди которых ещё и есть третья команда — мимик. Да и любой перс может купить маску в магазине и перевоплотиться в другого.

А ночью, ой, простите, в междумирье, ты даже не можешь отбиваться от заражённых .. игра тебе просто не даёт стрелять. А фотик работает с гигантским откатом. Зато мины можно ставить прямо на ходу, за секунду, прямо перед носом заражённого, и сбегать - умные мысли преследовали авторов, но они были быстрее. :D

Задумка второй части была интересной, но нуждается в глобальной переработке баланса и ролей. Также тут добавили режим Legacy из первой части, но это жалкая пародия с кучей визуальных багов и ненужных изменений карт, что отбивает желание в него играть.

Резюмирую. Хотите оживить игру и дать ей второй шанс? Перенесите режим Legacy из первой части для начала один в один, с полной копией геймплея и геометрии карт, хотя бы ночь сделайте такой же тёмной. Пофиксите баги.

Потом расширьте количество игроков для режима, а то шесть уже маловато. Добавьте новые предметы, например дефибриллятор или кислородную маску, чтобы можно было спасать игроков, погибших при переходе между локациями, это то чего так не хватало первой части.  

Но, конечно, шанс, что это увидят разработчики и прислушаются 0,0001 %. Так что помянем игру.
translated_text:
I'm a devoted fan of Deceit 1, not the latest build, but the Legacy version. I've played about three hundred hours of it and, in my opinion, experienced what was, in my opinion, the golden age of this game—2020.

I can't play this mode now because the developers shut down the servers. Yes, you can still log in to the latest build of the first game, but the Legacy mode doesn't work. Well, we decided to try the second game, which the developers were so eager to upgrade to.

What can I say? The graphics are a definite plus. Well, personally, I really enjoyed the visuals. But the gameplay... Yes, it seems like there are more roles, more opportunities, but in the end, you don't even have time to use half of them. You have to complete one hundred and fifty quests, while also monitoring altars and identifying infected, which also includes a third team—the Mimic. And any character can buy a mask in the store and transform into another character.

And at night, oh, sorry, in the interworld, you can't even fight off the infected... the game simply won't let you shoot. And the camera has a huge cooldown. But you can plant mines on the fly, in a second, right under the infected's nose, and run away—the developers were haunted by clever ideas, but they were faster. :D

The concept of the second part was interesting, but it needs a complete rework of the balance and roles. They also added the Legacy mode from the first part, but it's a pathetic parody with a bunch of visual bugs and unnecessary map changes, which makes it undesirable to play.

To summarize: Want to revive the game and give it a second chance? Start by porting the Legacy mode from the first part exactly, with a complete copy of the gameplay and map geometry, and at least make the night just as dark. Fix the bugs.

Then expand the number of players for this mode; six is ​​already too few. Add new items, like a defibrillator or oxygen mask, to help rescue players who die while moving between locations—that's something the first game sorely lacked.

But, of course, the chances that the developers will see this and take it into account are 0.0001%. So, let's remember the game.

# Chained Together – eine geniale Multiplayer-Idee, die spielerisch leider erstaunlich dünn bleibt

**Chained Together** gehört zu diesen Spielen, deren Konzept man innerhalb eines einzigen Satzes verstanden hat: Mehrere Spieler versuchen gemeinsam, aus der Hölle nach oben zu klettern – und sind dabei buchstäblich mit einer Kette aneinandergefesselt.

Das klingt herrlich absurd. Und tatsächlich entstehen daraus einige der lustigsten, frustrierendsten und chaotischsten Koop-Momente, die man mit Freunden haben kann.

Das eigentliche Problem von Chained Together zeigt sich allerdings relativ schnell:

**Die Idee ist deutlich besser als das Spiel, das darum gebaut wurde.**

Die Kette ist clever, das gemeinsame Scheitern kann unglaublich unterhaltsam sein und mit den richtigen Leuten entstehen fantastische Situationen. Aber sobald man den sozialen Faktor etwas aus der Gleichung nimmt und sich fragt, was Chained Together rein spielerisch eigentlich bietet, bleibt überraschend wenig übrig.

Im Kern ist es ein relativ einfacher 3D-Plattformer, dessen größte Besonderheit darin besteht, dass Fehler anderer Spieler zu den eigenen Fehlern werden.

Und das trägt nicht unbedingt über die gesamte Spielzeit.

## Das Grundkonzept ist zunächst hervorragend

Man beginnt in der Hölle und versucht, immer weiter nach oben zu gelangen.

Dabei springt, klettert und balanciert man über Plattformen, bewegliche Hindernisse und verschiedene Parcours. Im Koop-Modus sind bis zu vier Spieler miteinander verbunden. Das Spiel unterstützt sowohl lokalen als auch Online-Koop. Die Kette wird tatsächlich physikalisch simuliert und kann sich beispielsweise um Plattformen legen.

Genau diese Mechanik ist der Grund, warum Chained Together überhaupt funktioniert.

Wenn ein Spieler springt, müssen die anderen reagieren.

Wenn einer abrutscht, können die anderen ihn unter Umständen halten.

Wenn zwei Spieler unterschiedliche Vorstellungen davon haben, wann gesprungen werden soll, endet das Ganze häufig damit, dass plötzlich alle Beteiligten hundert Meter tiefer liegen.

Und genau das kann sehr lustig sein.

Zumindest die ersten Male.

Das Besondere ist nämlich weniger die Plattform selbst als das menschliche Chaos, das darum entsteht.

„Spring jetzt!“

„Nein, noch nicht!“

„WARUM SPRINGST DU?!“

„ICH DACHTE, DU SPRINGST AUCH!“

Und anschließend fliegen alle gemeinsam in die Tiefe.

In solchen Situationen zeigt Chained Together seine größte Stärke.

## Das Spiel wird hauptsächlich von den Mitspielern getragen

Das ist gleichzeitig aber auch mein größtes grundsätzliches Problem mit dem Spiel.

Viele gute Koop-Spiele funktionieren hervorragend **mit** Freunden.

Chained Together funktioniert teilweise überhaupt erst **wegen** der Freunde.

Das klingt ähnlich, ist aber ein wichtiger Unterschied.

Die unterhaltsamsten Momente entstehen meistens nicht deshalb, weil das Leveldesign besonders brillant wäre, sondern weil jemand einen Fehler macht, etwas falsch versteht oder die gesamte Gruppe versehentlich in den Abgrund zieht.

Auch andere Spieler beschreiben genau diesen Unterschied: Solo bleibt im Wesentlichen ein Hindernisparcours übrig, während Kommunikation, Timing und gegenseitiges Retten erst im Koop den eigentlichen Reiz erzeugen.

Mit drei guten Freunden kann Chained Together deshalb sehr unterhaltsam sein.

Alleine?

Da wird ziemlich schnell sichtbar, wie wenig Substanz hinter dem Grundkonzept steckt.

## Solo verliert Chained Together einen großen Teil seiner Identität

Das Spiel kann auch alleine gespielt werden. Einige Hindernisse werden dafür entsprechend angepasst.

Technisch funktioniert das.

Aber meiner Meinung nach stellt sich dann ziemlich schnell die Frage:

**Warum sollte ich Chained Together überhaupt alleine spielen?**

Ohne Mitspieler fällt die zentrale soziale Komponente praktisch vollständig weg.

Plötzlich ist es einfach ein weiterer 3D-Kletter-Plattformer, bei dem man von Plattform zu Plattform springt und bei Fehlern herunterfällt.

Die Kette, die eigentlich das Alleinstellungsmerkmal des Spiels ist, verliert damit einen großen Teil ihrer Bedeutung.

Natürlich kann man versuchen, Bestzeiten zu erreichen oder die Strecke möglichst sauber zu spielen.

Aber als reines Jump-'n'-Run ist Chained Together meiner Meinung nach nicht interessant genug, um dauerhaft zu motivieren.

Dafür fehlen sowohl spielerische Tiefe als auch wirklich außergewöhnliches Leveldesign.

## Die Kettenphysik ist gleichzeitig Stärke und Schwäche

Die Kette ist ohne Zweifel das interessanteste Element des Spiels.

Sie kann hervorragend funktionieren.

Ein Spieler fällt, während die anderen stehen bleiben und ihn halten.

Jemand schwingt an der Kette.

Die Gruppe versucht, einen schwierigen Sprung gemeinsam zu koordinieren.

Solche Momente sind großartig.

Das Problem ist nur:

Physikbasierte Spiele sind besonders dann problematisch, wenn sie gleichzeitig extrem präzise Bewegungen vom Spieler verlangen.

Und Chained Together möchte beides sein.

Das Spiel verlangt stellenweise exaktes Springen und gutes Timing, während gleichzeitig mehrere Figuren und eine physikalisch simulierte Kette Einfluss auf die Bewegung nehmen.

Dadurch fühlt sich ein Scheitern nicht immer verdient an.

Auch Spieler haben Situationen beschrieben, in denen die Kettenphysik unerwartete Kräfte erzeugt, Figuren ungewöhnlich stark beschleunigt oder bestimmte Bewegungen plötzlich Momentum verlieren. Ein weiterer wiederkehrender Kritikpunkt ist, dass die Kette trotz ihrer zentralen Rolle nicht konsequent mit allen Umgebungsobjekten interagiert.

Natürlich gehört Chaos zum Spiel.

Aber es gibt einen Unterschied zwischen:

**„Wir haben schlecht gespielt.“**

und

**„Was genau ist da gerade eigentlich passiert?“**

Letzteres kommt für meinen Geschmack zu häufig vor.

## Frust ist kein Nebeneffekt – Frust ist das Spielprinzip

Chained Together gehört eindeutig in die Kategorie der sogenannten Rage Games.

Das Spiel selbst bezeichnet den normalen Modus als entsprechend hart: Im Normal-Modus gibt es keine Rücksetz-Hilfe nach einem großen Sturz. Im Anfänger-Modus kann man sich dagegen zum höchsten zuvor erreichten Punkt zurückversetzen lassen. Zusätzlich gibt es einen Lava-Modus, bei dem man unter Zeitdruck vor aufsteigender Lava fliehen muss.

Damit weiß das Spiel grundsätzlich, was es sein möchte.

Das Problem ist also nicht, **dass** Chained Together frustrierend ist.

Das ist Absicht.

Die Frage ist vielmehr, ob der Frust immer interessant ist.

Und meiner Meinung nach lautet die Antwort: nein.

Wenn man nach einem anspruchsvollen Hindernis scheitert, weil man selbst den Sprung falsch eingeschätzt hat, kann das motivieren.

Wenn die gesamte Gruppe wegen eines missverständlichen Kommandos abstürzt, kann das sehr lustig sein.

Wenn man aber dieselben einfachen Passagen zum fünften oder sechsten Mal wiederholen muss, weil man sehr weit zurückgefallen ist, beginnt der Frust seinen spielerischen Zweck zu verlieren.

Dann ist die Wiederholung nicht mehr schwierig.

Sie ist einfach nur zeitaufwendig.

Das ist für mich ein entscheidender Unterschied.

## Große Rückfälle sind nicht automatisch gute Schwierigkeit

Chained Together lebt stark davon, dass ein kleiner Fehler enorme Konsequenzen haben kann.

Das erzeugt Spannung.

Wenn man bereits weit oben ist und weiß, dass ein schlechter Sprung einen massiven Rückfall bedeuten kann, wird selbst eine scheinbar einfache Plattform plötzlich nervenaufreibend.

Das funktioniert.

Aber irgendwann entsteht ein anderes Problem:

Die Strafe steht nicht mehr im Verhältnis zur eigentlichen Herausforderung.

Ein Fehler von zwei Sekunden kann dazu führen, dass man mehrere Minuten bekannten Content erneut spielen muss.

Beim ersten Mal ist das dramatisch.

Beim zweiten Mal vielleicht noch lustig.

Beim fünften Mal ist es hauptsächlich lästig.

# Chained Together – a brilliant multiplayer idea that, unfortunately, remains surprisingly thin in terms of gameplay

**Chained Together** is one of those games whose concept you can grasp in a single sentence: Several players try to climb out of hell together – and are literally chained to each other.

That sounds wonderfully absurd. And indeed, it creates some of the funniest, most frustrating, and most chaotic co-op moments you can have with friends.

However, the real problem with Chained Together becomes apparent relatively quickly:

**The idea is significantly better than the game built around it.**

The chain is clever, the shared failures can be incredibly entertaining, and fantastic situations arise with the right people. But as soon as you take the social factor out of the equation and ask yourself what Chained Together actually offers in terms of gameplay, surprisingly little remains.

At its core, it's a relatively simple 3D platformer whose most distinctive feature is that other players' mistakes become your own.

And that doesn't necessarily hold up for the entire duration of the game.

## The basic concept is initially excellent.

You start in Hell and try to climb ever higher.

You jump, climb, and balance across platforms, moving obstacles, and various courses. In co-op mode, up to four players are connected. The game supports both local and online co-op. The chain is actually simulated physically and can, for example, wrap itself around platforms.

This mechanic is precisely why Chained Together works at all.

When one player jumps, the others have to react.

If someone slips, the others can potentially catch them.

If two players have different ideas about when to jump, the whole thing often ends with everyone suddenly lying a hundred meters below.

And that can be very funny.

At least the first few times.

The special thing isn't so much the platform itself, but the human chaos that ensues around it.

"Jump now!"

"No, not yet!"

"WHY ARE YOU JUMPING?!"

"I THOUGHT YOU WERE JUMPING TOO!"

And then they all plummet into the abyss together.

It's in situations like these that Chained Together demonstrates its greatest strength.

## The game is primarily driven by the other players

But that's also my biggest fundamental problem with the game.

Many good co-op games work brilliantly **with** friends.

Chained Together only works, in part, **because** of friends.

That sounds similar, but it's a crucial difference.

The most entertaining moments usually don't arise because the level design is particularly brilliant, but because someone makes a mistake, misunderstands something, or accidentally pulls the entire group into the abyss.

Other players describe precisely this difference: playing solo is essentially just an obstacle course, while communication, timing, and mutual rescue only create the real appeal in co-op.

With three good friends, Chained Together can therefore be very entertaining.

Alone?

It quickly becomes apparent how little substance lies behind the basic concept.

## Chained Together loses a large part of its identity when played solo

The game can also be played alone. Some obstacles are adapted accordingly.

Technically, this works.

But in my opinion, the question quickly arises:

**Why should I even play Chained Together alone?**

Without other players, the central social component practically disappears.

Suddenly, it's just another 3D climbing platformer where you jump from platform to platform and fall off if you make a mistake.

The chain, which is actually the game's unique selling point, loses a large part of its significance.

Of course, you can try to achieve best times or play the course as cleanly as possible.

But as a pure jump-'n'-run game, Chained Together isn't interesting enough to provide lasting motivation, in my opinion.

It lacks both gameplay depth and truly exceptional level design.

## Chain Physics: Both a Strength and a Weakness

The chain is undoubtedly the most interesting element of the game.

It can work brilliantly.

One player falls while the others stand and catch them.

Someone swings on the chain.

The group tries to coordinate a difficult jump together.

Moments like these are fantastic.

The problem is:

Physics-based games are particularly problematic when they simultaneously demand extremely precise movements from the player.

And Chained Together aims to be both.

The game sometimes requires exact jumps and good timing, while multiple characters and a physically simulated chain influence the movement.

As a result, failure doesn't always feel deserved.

Players have also described situations where the chain physics generates unexpected forces, characters accelerate unusually strongly, or certain movements suddenly lose momentum. Another recurring criticism is that, despite its central role, the chain doesn't consistently interact with all environmental objects.

Of course, chaos is part of the game.

But there's a difference between:

**"We played badly."**

and

**"What exactly just happened?"**

The latter comes up far too often for my liking.

## Frustration isn't a side effect – frustration is the game's core principle

Chained Together clearly belongs in the category of so-called rage games.

The game itself describes the normal mode as correspondingly difficult: In normal mode, there's no reset assistance after a big fall. In beginner mode, on the other hand, you can be reset to the highest point you've previously reached. There's also a Lava mode where you have to escape rising lava under time pressure.

So the game basically knows what it wants to be.

The problem isn't **that** Chained Together is frustrating.

That's intentional.

The real question is whether the frustration is always interesting.

And in my opinion, the answer is: no.


Failing after a challenging obstacle because you misjudged the jump can be motivating.

When the whole group crashes due to a misunderstood command, it can be hilarious.

But when you have to repeat the same easy sections for the fifth or sixth time because you've fallen far behind, the frustration starts to lose its purpose.

Then the repetition isn't difficult anymore.

It's simply time-consuming.

That's a crucial difference for me.

## Big setbacks don't automatically equal good difficulty

Chained Together thrives on the fact that a small mistake can have enormous consequences.

This creates tension.

When you're already high up and know that a bad jump can mean a massive setback, even a seemingly easy platform suddenly becomes nerve-wracking.

This works.

But at some point, another problem arises:

The punishment is no longer proportionate to the actual challenge.

A two-second mistake can force you to replay several minutes of familiar content.

The first time, it's dramatic.

The second time, maybe still funny.

By the fifth time, it's mostly just annoying.

review_text:
Pico Park es, sin duda alguna el JUEGO DEFINITIVO para cualquiera que decida que tiene muchos amigos y necesita deshacerse de ellos inmediatamente. El diseño de niveles parece fríamente calculado para que el amigo con la peor conexión a internet y reflejos arruine el progreso de los otros siete jugadores, también me hizo empatizar con Subaru de Re: Zero, porque  ver a tus amigos cometer el mismo error y volver a morir en un bucle infinito es un sufrimiento psicológico que parece sacado del IF de la Codicia.

Calificación 8/10 No lo vuelvo a jugar nunca (a menos que nos juntemos otra vez otra noche xd)
translated_text:
Pico Park is, without a doubt, THE ULTIMATE GAME for anyone who decides they have too many friends and needs to get rid of them immediately. The level design seems coldly calculated so that the friend with the worst internet connection and reflexes ruins the progress of the other seven players. It also made me empathize with Subaru from Re:Zero, because watching your friends make the same mistake and die again in an infinite loop is psychological torture that seems straight out of the "If" scenario of Greed.

Rating 8/10 I'm never playing it again (unless we get together again another night lol)

A última tela dele foi uma virada de chave na minha mente. Enquanto todos amigos estavam a frente, se matando... Eu estava tentando entender o porque avançar enquanto as coisas vão vir.
No final das contas, a vida vai acontecer e você não precisa acelerar o rumo dos eventos, os monstros vão aparecer, os desafios vão ser resolvidos. E porque sofrer por tudo isso? Se desprender da ansiedade resultou no meu novo eu.

Obrigado meus amigos, obrigado a todos que estão lendo.
Saibam que a experiência desse jogo ser satânica é algo totalmente dependente de VOCÊ.

Dito isso 10/10.
Nunca mais vou jogar essa desgraça KK

Thank you my friends, thank you to everyone who is reading.

Know that the experience of this game being satanic is something totally dependent on YOU.

That said, 10/10.

I'm never playing this damn thing again LOL

Crab Game is not merely a free-to-play multiplayer release; it is a staggering, avant-garde dissertation on the human condition under the crushing weight of hyper-competitive modern society. Released in 2021 by the singular auteur known simply as Dani, the title fiercely asserts its originality, boldly declaring itself "definitely not based on any online streaming pop culture Korean TV shows" to avoid legal constraints and, more importantly, to establish its own sovereign artistic identity. What masquerades as a chaotic assortment of digital playground activities is, in truth, a profound interactive tragedy.

The visual and auditory design of Crab Game is a masterclass in deliberate brutalism. While pedestrian critics might dismiss the unpolished, aggressively lo-fi Unity-engine aesthetic as "janky," true connoisseurs recognise it as a brilliant subversion of the industry's shallow obsession with hyper-realism. The blocky, stark geometry of its 28 maps strips away all superfluous comfort, leaving only the raw, pulsating core of Hobbesian survival. Furthermore, the implementation of proximity chat is nothing short of an auditory theatre of the absurd. By forcing participants to endure the unfiltered screams, breathless betrayals, and desperate pleas of up to 34 other souls, the developer holds a terrifying mirror up to the chaotic noise of human existence. You do not just play this game; you survive a panopticon of moral decay.

Mechanically, the genius of the experience lies in its devastating critique of how the innocence of youth is commodified into ruthless bloodsport. The ludic loop centres on childhood pastimes, tag, hide-and-seek, and floor-is-lava variants, corrupted into lethal zero-sum arenas. Eliminating a nameless, identically dressed peer with a sickeningly blunt "slap" mechanic or a discarded pipe forces the player to grapple with their own complicity in a dog-eat-dog hierarchy. Every frantic jump across a fragile glass bridge is a heart-stopping meditation on trust's fragility. Every frantic scramble to steal a crown before the timer hits zero is a searing indictment of corporate ladder-climbing.

Ultimately, Crab Game asks a singular, haunting question: What are we willing to do to our fellow man for a fleeting, intangible victory? Dani has not simply coded a battle royale; he has crafted a high-art sociology experiment. It is a triumphant, visceral masterpiece that leaves its players forever changed, staring blankly into the abyss of their own morality as the post-match scoreboard fades to black.

review_text:
Fun, Strategic, and Beautifully Chaotic (But Keep an Eye on the Bugs)Overall Rating: Recommended (7/10 solo, 5/10 multiplayer due to bugs)Chef Life: A Restaurant Simulator strikes a great balance between deep management and the frantic, chaotic fun of running a kitchen. It's an indie gem with a lot of heart, though it is currently held back by some rough technical edges.
THE GOOD: Satisfying Progression: Career Mode starts you with a small diner inherited from your father. Unlocking recipes, buying equipment across three unique stores, and building up to high-pressure "Gourmet Chef" boss battles creates an addicting gameplay loop. Smart Menu Strategy: The "Food Tag" system (like Fast Food or Bakery) adds great strategy. Linking tags grants massive perks—for example, stacking Bakery items lets your dishes yield 5 to 6 servings instead of the base 4, making service much smoother. Excellent Bakery DLC: A fantastic change of pace from the main game. It takes you to a Parisian bakery where you handle everything from baking Sourdough and Baguettes to serving coffee and running the cash register .Great Co-op Potential: In multiplayer, splitting the menu allows you to maximize early-game growth and tackle complex dishes that would overwhelm a solo player.
THE BAD (Bugs & Glitches)While the core game is fantastic, the technical issues—especially in multiplayer—can be frustrating: Progress-Killing Reload Bug: Saved items in the fridge can break upon reloading. Fully baked cakes or pies (which give 8 plates) frequently reset into raw dough, destroying hours of prep and occasionally forcing a total save restart.The "Moving Day" Void: Upgrading to a larger restaurant is a gamble. The large transition box meant to hold your utensils and spices routinely glitches out, deleting 15–20 of your items permanently and forcing you to re-shop from scratch.Interactable Object Glitches: Food inside fridges will randomly become un-interactable. If a reload doesn't fix it, your ingredients are trapped, forcing you to waste money re-buying them. Duplication glitches also leave random plates cluttering the floor. Broken AI Pathfinding: Dropping furniture near walls can clip items out-of-bounds. If a plate rack clips, your AI waiters will literally walk out of the map to return dishes, abandoning their dining room duties and leaving you to panic-cook and wait tables simultaneously.

Final Verdict: Highly recommended if you are playing solo, as you will encounter far fewer bugs. If you play multiplayer, just be prepared for some frustrating technical hiccups. It's a fantastic indie project.

review_text:
Supermarket Together - это кооперативный симулятор управления супермаркетом, который ворвался в чарты Steam благодаря своей доступности и возможности играть в огромной компании.

---

 О чем игра?
Вы (один или с друзьями до 16 человек) открываете пустой склад, который должен превратиться в процветающий гипермаркет. Вам нужно:
1.  Заказывать товары через компьютер.
2.  Раскладывать их по полкам.
3.  Выставлять ценники (желательно не слишком грабительские).
4.  Пробивать товары на кассе.
5.  Бить воришек метлой (это важная часть геймплея).

---

Плюсы (Почему это весело)

1.  Кооперативный хаос: В отличие от одиночных симуляторов, здесь работа распределяется. Кто-то работает «логистом» на складе, кто-то - бессменный кассир, а кто-то бегает по залу и следит за порядком. В компании друзей игра превращается в забавный балаган.
2.  Дерево навыков (Перки): В игре есть система прогрессии. Зарабатывая опыт, вы открываете очки навыков, которые позволяют расширять магазин, лицензировать новые продукты или улучшать характеристики персонажа. Это дает четкую цель.
4.  Простота: Механики интуитивно понятны. Вам не нужно читать мануалы, чтобы понять, как работает сканер или как выставить цену.

---

Минусы (Честно о недостатках)

1.  Техническое состояние (Кривизна): Игра выглядит и ощущается как типичный проект на Unity «из коробок». Анимации топорные, физика предметов иногда сходит с ума, а персонажи двигаются максимально неестественно.
2.  Однообразие (Гринд): Спустя 3-4 часа геймплейный цикл замыкается. Вы делаете одно и то же: коробка - полка - касса. Если у вас нет цели открыть абсолютно все товары, игра может быстро надоесть.
3.  Экономический дисбаланс: На определенных этапах денег становится слишком много, и вызов пропадает. Либо, наоборот, из-за пары ошибок в ценах можно уйти в крутое пике.
4.  Воришки: Сначала бить их метлой весело, но со временем это начинает раздражать, так как они отвлекают от основных процессов.

---

 Сравнение с Supermarket Simulator
Если оригинальный Supermarket Simulator — это более медитативный, залипательный процесс для одного, то Supermarket Together создана исключительно для мультиплеера. В соло она проигрывает оригиналу по глубине и проработке деталей.

Итоговый вердикт

Supermarket Together - это отличный «таймкиллер» для компании друзей. Она не претендует на звание серьезного симулятора, но дарит массу эмоций именно за счет взаимодействия игроков.
Стоит ли играть одному? Скорее нет, быстро станет скучно.
Стоит ли играть с друзьями? Определенно да. Это бесплатно, весело и позволяет на пару вечеров почувствовать себя сплоченной командой (или разругаться из-за неправильно расставленного молока).
translated_text:
Supermarket Together is a co-op supermarket management simulator that has stormed the Steam charts thanks to its accessibility and the ability to play in large groups.

---

What's the game about?
You (alone or with up to 16 friends) open an empty warehouse and turn it into a thriving hypermarket. You need to:
1. Order products via the computer.
2. Stock them on the shelves.
3. Set price tags (preferably not too exorbitant ones).
4. Scan products at the checkout.
5. Beat thieves with a broom (this is an important part of the gameplay).

---

Pros (Why it's fun)

1. Co-op chaos: Unlike single-player simulators, the work is divided. Someone works as a "logistics" in the warehouse, someone is a permanent cashier, and someone else runs around the floor keeping order. With a group of friends, the game turns into a hilarious mess.
2. Skill Tree (Perks): The game has a progression system. By earning experience, you unlock skill points that allow you to expand the store, license new products, or improve your character's stats. This gives you a clear goal.
4. Simplicity: The mechanics are intuitive. You don't need to read manuals to understand how the scanner works or how to set a price.

---

Cons (Honestly about the flaws)

1. Technical Condition (Curvature): The game looks and feels like a typical Unity project out of the box. The animations are crude, the physics of objects sometimes go crazy, and the characters move in a very unnatural way.
2. Monotony (Grind): After 3-4 hours, the gameplay loop becomes monotonous. You do the same thing: box - shelf - checkout. If you don't have a goal to open absolutely every product, the game can quickly become boring. 3. Economic Imbalance: At certain points, the money becomes too much, and the challenge disappears. Or, conversely, a couple of pricing errors can send you into a steep decline.
4. Thieves: At first, beating them with a broom is fun, but over time it becomes annoying, as they distract from the main process.

---

Comparison with Supermarket Simulator
While the original Supermarket Simulator is a more meditative, engaging experience for single-player, Supermarket Together is designed exclusively for multiplayer. In solo play, it lacks the depth and detail of the original.

Final Verdict

Supermarket Together is an excellent time-killer for a group of friends. It doesn't pretend to be a serious simulator, but it delivers a lot of excitement thanks to the interaction between players.
Is it worth playing alone? Probably not; it gets boring quickly.
Is it worth playing with friends? Definitely yes. It's free, fun, and allows you to feel like a team for a couple of evenings (or to quarrel over misplaced milk).

review_text:
«Ну что, пошли отрабатывать смену в маркете?» - примерно с таких слов начиналась каждая сессия в эту игру с подругой. И в целом, это лучше всего передаёт её суть :)

Игре я поставлю пальчик вверх: для любителей подобного рода симуляторов она вполне зайдёт, в особенности если играть в приятной компании. Лично мне же после часов так 45-50 игра всё-таки наскучила – когда переходишь из роли кассира/охранника/уборщика/и-прочее к роли простого администратора и логиста, в игре делать становиться нечего. Включаешь день и ждёшь пока он закончится, чтобы обновить список товаров и кулинарии на ускорении и начать всё сначала. В какой-то момент даже появилось чувство, что ускорение во время рабочего дня тоже было бы не лишним (и то, только для того чтобы закрыть всё древо развития, так бы с этим не заморачивались). Ивент на пришельцев был небольшим разнообразием, но тоже не очень надолго. 

Из того что прямо совсем не понравилось – стенд «логистики». По его описанию можно было предположить, что благодаря этому стенду можно из классической карты перебросить средства на Плазу – и там быстренько заново обустроить свой магазин. На деле, передавать можно только по 1000 в день, что на самом деле вообще ни о чём. Добивать достижения в Плазе оказалось тем ещё испытанием… Наша упёртость победила, но ощущения от этого несколько смазались, тем более что планировка самой Плазы после классики показалась очень неудобной.
translated_text:
"So, are we off to work our shift at the market?" - that's roughly how every session of this game with my friend began. And overall, that's the best way to describe it :)

I'll give the game a thumbs up: for fans of this kind of simulator, it's perfectly enjoyable, especially if you play with a good group of friends. Personally, after about 45-50 hours, I finally got bored – when you transition from being a cashier/security guard/janitor/etc. to a simple administrator and logistician, there's nothing to do. You start a day and wait for it to end, so you can refresh your inventory and cooking lists at full speed and start all over again. At one point, I even felt like a speed boost during the workday would have been nice (and only to complete the entire development tree; they wouldn't have bothered with it anyway). The alien event was a bit of a change, but it didn't last very long.

One thing I really didn't like was the "logistics" stand. Its description suggested that this stand would allow you to transfer funds from your classic card to the Plaza, allowing you to quickly refurbish your store there. In reality, you can only transfer 1,000 per day, which is really nothing special. Reaching Plaza achievements turned out to be quite a challenge... Our stubbornness prevailed, but it somewhat dampened the impression, especially since the Plaza's layout seemed very inconvenient after the classic one.

Overcooked 2 es una experiencia muy linda. Genuinamente creo que llegó en el momento adecuado a mi vida. Con el paso de los niveles, entiendes la importancia de trabajar en equipo y lo imprescindible que es comunicarte con los demás para lograr hacer bien las recetas y cumplir con los puntos necesarios en el tiempo solicitado.

Cuando gritas "cut, cut" o "clean dishes" a tu compañero, el juego te enseña a dar instrucciones precisas, rápidas y directas. Es el mismo tipo de coordinación ágil que te salva la vida en los últimos minutos de un hackathon o cuando los plazos de un proyecto en grupo se te vienen encima.

También aprendes a optimizar procesos coordinando roles como quién corta, quién cocina y quién lava platos para evitar cuellos de botella y manejar múltiples tareas en paralelo para maximizar la entrega de órdenes.

Esta dinámica pone a prueba tu adaptabilidad para resolver distintos problemas como cuando la cocina se divide, las plataformas se mueven o el mapa se incendia. Nuestro cerebro aprende a descartar el plan original y a reasignar roles en milisegundos sin paralizarse.

E indiscutiblemente se desarrolla conciencia espacial y diseño de flujo. Esquivar a tus compañeros, aprovechar las cintas transportadoras y lanzar ingredientes por encima de abismos entrena tu percepción del entorno. Acostumbras al ojo a entender cómo la distribución de los elementos afecta la eficiencia del usuario.

Y recordar el valor de la tolerancia a la frustración y el control emocional. Perder la tercera estrella en el último segundo por entregar un plato equivocado y entender que hay que repetirlo porque se necesita practicar más o quizás buscar otra estrategia, nos recuerda la importancia de la paciencia y de disfrutar el proceso, no solo el resultado. En fin, es un juego.

Me divertí un montón, aprendí muchísimo y sin duda me encantó. Lo recomiendo totalmente si quieres pasar un buen rato con tu familia, pareja o amigos; es una experiencia imprescindible para quienes nos gustan los juegos cooperativos que te retan a meterle cabeza y trabajar bajo presión.
translated_text:
Overcooked 2 is a wonderful experience. I genuinely believe it came into my life at the perfect time. As you progress through the levels, you understand the importance of teamwork and how crucial communication is to successfully complete recipes and meet deadlines.

When you yell "cut, cut" or "clean dishes" to your teammate, the game teaches you to give precise, quick, and direct instructions. It's the same kind of agile coordination that saves your life in the final minutes of a hackathon or when a group project deadline is looming.

You also learn to optimize processes by coordinating roles like who chops, who cooks, and who washes dishes to avoid bottlenecks and manage multiple tasks simultaneously to maximize order fulfillment.

This dynamic tests your adaptability to solve various problems, such as when the kitchen splits, platforms shift, or the map catches fire. Our brains learn to discard the original plan and reassign roles in milliseconds without freezing up.

And it undeniably develops spatial awareness and flow design skills. Dodging your teammates, using conveyor belts, and throwing ingredients over gaps trains your perception of the environment. You train your eye to understand how the distribution of elements affects user efficiency.

And remember the value of frustration tolerance and emotional control. Losing the third star at the last second for delivering the wrong dish and understanding that you have to repeat it because you need more practice or perhaps a different strategy, reminds us of the importance of patience and enjoying the process, not just the result. In short, it's a game.

I had a blast, learned a ton, and absolutely loved it. I highly recommend it if you want to have a good time with your family, partner, or friends; it's an essential experience for those of us who enjoy cooperative games that challenge you to think critically and work under pressure.

review_text:
Have you ever walked into a space where every little detail has been thoughtfully designed? Where you can tell that whoever made the space loved every potential visitor and wanted them to have the best experience possible?

That's this game. 

It's not just about thoughtful level and puzzle design (although you will definitely find that also) , but it's details like the sound design. As a fellow Aussie, the sounds of the birds in the dawn and the frogs in the evening filled my heart with comfort. I loved details like the sound of the squeaky sand. Features like a day/night cycle that presents both advantages and challenges, but never lasts long enough for it to be burdensome. The fact that you can get lost easily, but getting lost is absolutely okay and even sometimes desirable. The many opportunities for nonsense! The fact there is no hurry, no predetermined way to play the game. 

Every little detail in this game has been made with love for the humans who play it and I am grateful for the experience.

Jsem téměř s jistotou schopný říct, že Big Walk je nejlepší coop hra letošního roku. Ovšem to ale neznamená, že tahle walking simulator puzzle hra z pohledu první osoby, nemá žádné chyby. Má a jsou celkem zásadní.

Big walk je puzzle walking simulator s proximity voice chatem, s tím že hra počítá že jí budete hrát bez externího zdroje komunikace. Ve velkém množství puzzlů rozeseté v openworldu hry figuruje neverbální komunikace, pomocí emotů či jiných nápověd. Tady přichází i první kritika. Některé puzzly vůbec nepůsobí jako puzzly, ale spíše nutnost jít přes celou mapu a sbírat určité předměty. Pro převoz mapy můžete použít vláček či lanovku nebo rozsáhlý tunelový systém pod zemí, hra tedy nemá žádný fast travel a ani žádnou přehlednější mapu, kromě té uprostřed mapy, kterou si ale nemůžete vzít s sebou.

Při traverzi světa se budou hodit různé itemy, ať už to jsou kompasy, vysílačky, světlice, či lampy na svícení. A budou se velmi hodit, day/night cyklus ve hře je totiž možná až příliš rychlý a ve hře není v podstatě žádný puzzle co by plně využíval noci. Tedy noc se stane spíše frustrující kulisou.

Absence inventáře je taky menší problém, můžete nosit totiž jenom jeden item v ruce. Můžete nacházet batohy na mapě, ale nemůžete s ním operovat. Potřebujete druhého hráče aby vám dal a sundaval itemy z něj.

Big walk je i přes některé zvláštní designové rozhodnutí naprosto skvělá relaxační coop hra pro vás a vaše kamarády. Inventář a nastavení pro změnu délky dne a více různorodých puzzlů by ale šikly.
translated_text:
I can almost say with certainty that Big Walk is the best coop game of this year. However, that doesn't mean that this walking simulator puzzle game from a first-person perspective doesn't have any flaws. It does, and they are quite fundamental.

Big Walk is a puzzle walking simulator with proximity voice chat, with the game counting on you playing it without an external source of communication. A large number of puzzles scattered throughout the game's open world feature non-verbal communication, using emotes or other hints. This is where the first criticism comes in. Some puzzles don't feel like puzzles at all, but rather the need to go across the entire map and collect certain items. To transport the map, you can use a train or a cable car or an extensive tunnel system underground, so the game has no fast travel or any more clearly arranged map, except for the one in the middle of the map, which you can't take with you.

Various items will come in handy when traversing the world, be it compasses, walkie-talkies, flares, or lamps for lighting. And they will be very useful, the day/night cycle in the game is perhaps too fast and there is basically no puzzle in the game that would fully utilize the night. So the night becomes a rather frustrating backdrop.

The absence of inventory is also a minor problem, as you can only carry one item in your hand. You can find backpacks on the map, but you cannot operate them. You need a second player to give you and take items from them.

Despite some strange design decisions, Big Walk is an absolutely great relaxing coop game for you and your friends. Inventory and settings for changing the length of the day and more diverse puzzles would be nice.

パズルが幾つかあるのですが、そのほとんどは声による伝達を阻害されていて、代わりの方法で伝達する必要があります。

これが、ほんとうに伝わらない。
パズル自体は簡単めなものが多いのですが、「声」という武器がひとつ使えないだけで、難易度は爆上がりです。

オープンワールド的なところにパズルが点在しているタイプのゲームで、移動にも割と時間がかかります。
その間に、さっき解いたパズルの感想や文句を言ったり。なんとなくな雑談をしたり。どう攻略するか話し合ったり、、、。

パズルで話せなくなる分、めちゃくちゃ移動中に話すことができますが、これも楽しかったです。

〇可愛いキャラクター
木の人形のような、なんともいえないキャラクターがとてもかわいいです。
遠くで、手をパタパタさせて「ここだよー」って伝えてる感じとか、すごくいいです。

□まとめ
マルチで遊べるパズルゲームとして、中々の完成度だと思います。
仲のいい友達4人くらいと、固定で遊ぶと盛り上がったり喧嘩すること？間違いなしです。
ぜひぜひ、遊んでみてください。

review_text:
This was a very fun (2 player lobby) game to play with my friend. It was certainly not without it's moments of frustration but that was to be expected with us playing the bulk of it within a couple of weeks of it launching, and the majority of those issues have been resolved by now.
The map and mechanics where introduced very well in the tutorial area and allowed navigating the main game puzzles feel natural. Each of the modes of transportation were used more than once and didn't feel like a waste of time to unlock. The ending was a very genuine, full circle moment, as was ending+. The sometimes goofy physics meant that things like accidentally dropping the bocce ball on the ski lift and crying laughing after panicking and failing to retrieve it happened and frankly made our day.
However, if I never have to do a blind puzzle again I will be happy.
I recommend to people who want a good vibey friend game to play with a bit of puzzle but a lot of free time in between to catch up and just yap. Communication is key and yapping is required. Go in blind.
