Первые несколько игровых дней было интересно, потом всё скатывается в рутину. Я ещё застал те времена, когда о цифровом рынке мало слышали, а диски (в том числе пиратские) приходилось покупать. На Западе, видимо, ситуация обстояла иначе, потому что атмосфера игры не соответствует действительности. Если вы надеетесь поймать привкус ностальгии, то проходите мимо.     Здесь чересчур много свободного пространства, в то время как в настоящих магазинах оно преимущественно заставлено полками- места мало, но глазу есть за что зацепиться. Музыкальное сопровождение успело наскучить. Ещё тут зачем-то добавили барыгу с фильмами определённого содержания, правда, спросом эти фильмы пользовались от силы 3-4 дня. Даже после открытия всего инструментария в залах царит откровенное запустение относительно их масштабов, если не считать частых посетителей.  
И всё-таки ставлю игре "лайк". Она яркая, медитативная, может убить несколько вечеров. Интересно проводить дни ивента, когда меняется окружение, один раз даже ночью салют прогремел, это было волшебно. В пятницу 13 люди в масках Джексона спавнятся в магазине. Впервые  я заметил их, когда они стояли снаружи магазина и через витрину пялились на меня. Признаться, на секунду-две это даже показалось жутким. 
В целом, рекомендую игру как убивалку времени, но не как возможность вдохнуть того воздуха с ароматом пластика от коробки с DVD диском или видеокассетой.
translated_text:
The first few days of play were interesting, but then everything descended into routine. I remember the days when the digital market was unheard of, and you had to buy discs (including pirated ones). Things were apparently different in the West, because the game's atmosphere doesn't match reality. If you're hoping for a taste of nostalgia, you'll miss it. There's too much open space here, while in real stores it's mostly filled with shelves—small space, but plenty of eye-catching objects. The music has become boring. They also added a vendor selling movies of a certain genre for some reason, though these films were only in demand for 3-4 days. Even after unlocking all the tools, the rooms feel downright deserted relative to their size, except for frequent visitors. 
And yet, I give the game a thumbs up. It's bright, meditative, and can kill a few evenings. It's interesting to spend the event days, as the environment changes. One time, fireworks even went off at night, which was magical. On Friday the 13th, people in Jackson masks spawn in the store. I first noticed them when they were standing outside the store, staring at me through the display case. I admit, for a second or two, it even seemed creepy.
Overall, I recommend the game as a time-killer, but not as an opportunity to breathe in that plastic-scented air from a DVD or VHS case.

As much as it hurts to say, but in the current state I cant recommend the game.
Its good on a technical level, no game breaking bugs, UI is good enough, graphics are fine for this kind of game,  everything works, but the gameplay loop is lacking.
The game is fun for the first few hours but quickly starts to become more of a chore than a cozy sim game.
Some things that kinda annoyed me after a while:
- the gameplay loop more or less is the same from day one. While you unlock more stuff to sell, theres no real depth in anything you do. Decorations seem to not impact sales in any way. Sorting your vhs by genre or smth doesnt do anything. Theres no way to see if a customer is a regular or a new person.
- the handling of customers is not really great. If they need to pay fees theres a chance for them to throw their purchase on the ground and just leave, which is infuriating tbh. Just because you dont like fees doesnt mean youre allowed to just not pay it, especially for a broken vhs. Its double annoying if it happens like 3 times in a span of 5 minutes. 
Also sometimes they ask for a movie, which is fine itself, but sometimes they ask for lets say any romance movie, while standing in the romance sections with 3 shelves full of romance movies.
- you can hire people but theyre always gonna be much slower than you are. Even if theyre good in their respective category, theyre still slow.
- you dont have much control of anything really. Decorating is mediocre at best, a set selection of things and not much customisation. You cant have sales on your own (like giving 20% of romance rentals if your shelves are full or smth). No regular bonuses/stampcards thingies. 

So yeah, while it has potential, with the current price tag I would not recommend it. Maybe on a heavy sale or if they add more stuff in the future and deepen the gameplay aspects.

This is my first ever review and it honestly couldn't be for a more deserving game. I loved this game and so did my chat. Everyone was so engaged from the moment we played the demo till I got the full release not a few minutes later.

I really did hit a good nostalgic chord with me. I remember that feeling I used to get whenever it was time to head over to the local video store. If it was a smaller mom and pop shop they had a bunch of lesser known titles and the ever elusive spicy section in the back. It really was a magical experience to be able to yap about the movies with the folks at the counter to get recommendations or just gush about film.

I found myself trying to recreate that experiences in the game with the layout and the movie titles we would get. Chat and I looked forward to every Tuesday/Thursday to see what new titles we'd get. I loved the clever way the new releases were titled, I've seen so many of them it was like another hit of the nostalgia bomb. 

Pros:
I just loved the game, the gameplay loop was rewarding whether you were checking videos back in our checking folks out at the register. Honestly the entire game, the design, the movies, the layout of the store, everything gets a 10/10 for me. Worth every penny and all the hours I've put into it so far.

Cons: 
After max level, I'm not sure what else to do. I really really enjoying reaching goals in game and now I feel like I've gotten all the ones I can. It would be nice to add some genre achievements. 
I loved the special events but I was frustrated that I couldn't really do much during them, they just felt l like set dressing that felt a bit hollow at times.
I fired my best employee and I'm sad we can't get her back ;-;
The musical track felt a bit repetitive at times.

Suggestions:
I played this game on stream and was roleplaying my way through the game as a manger of the store. It would be nice to give the employees a bit of a boost with a "Great Job" action on the selection menu. Anything that gives them a plus X modifier to their performance. Could be nice for those with employees with "not great" states.
More achievements for holo movies / collecting a certain amount of movies.
There needs to be an easier way to be able to check through your store inventory.
Documentaries! 
Employee uniforms or letting them come in wearing 90s flannel! We need more flannel!

I heard some rumors about video games coming as a later update, I'm excited for it! Especially looking forward to the clever titles and covers.

review_text: Highly Recommended — 14.1 hours on record If you ever set foot inside a Blockbuster as a kid, this game is a pure, unadulterated nostalgia trip. Most simulator games on Steam feel like soulless, copy-paste asset flips, but Retro Rewind has an incredible amount of heart and effort put into it. After 14 hours, I am completely hooked on the cozy, addictive gameplay loop. What makes it great: The '90s Vibe: The developers nailed the aesthetic perfectly. From the neon signs and ugly carpets to the background ambient sounds, it completely captures that era. Hilarious Movie Parodies: The procedurally generated movie titles and hand-drawn covers are easily one of the best parts of the game. I’ve spent way too much time laughing at the ridiculous titles and parodies. Satisfying Management: Ordering movie bundles, sorting them by genre, setting up slushy and popcorn machines, and expanding the shop feels incredibly rewarding. Immersive Mechanics: The physical interactions feel tactile and deliberate. Dealing with the "be kind, rewind" rule, chasing down late fees, and waiting for the shady back-alley bootleg tape dealer on Tuesdays and Thursdays adds so much flavor. Customization: Being able to load your own video files to play on the TV behind the counter is an amazing touch. It runs flawlessly, has a ton of charm, and the developers are actively supporting it with content updates. It is easily worth the price of admission if you want a casual, laid-back management game to zone out to.

review_text:
Have to say, this is a very pretty game, but it's fairly shallow when it comes to its systems.

I managed to 100% the game and eventually reached the point where I was selling everything off as if I was closing the store down. There's simply not that much to do once you've seen most of what the game offers. The gameplay can become repetitive, and even the faster workers don't feel particularly fast.

The customisation is probably the strongest part of the game. If you enjoy decorating your store, arranging things and making the place look nice, there's plenty to play around with. Unfortunately, the decorations don't seem to have much impact on the actual gameplay or bring in significantly more customers.

The other issue is progression. Once you reach a certain point, you can end up with so many customers that they're basically just standing around waiting inside the store. It makes the whole thing feel more like managing a queue than running a shop.

I'd recommend picking it up on sale. It's a fun little game and looks great, but I wouldn't expect to get hundreds of hours out of it unless you particularly enjoy the decorating and customisation side of things.

review_text:
There is a lot this does right, but also a lot that it does wrong which ends up spoiling it for it.

The wrong:
1) Employees are too few, and too late. Level 10, then nothing until 20... So you are left doing almost ALL of the work until max level.
2) Employee automation is garbage. You can't assign primary and secondary jobs. You have to CONSTANTLY redirect them from one station to another.
3) Income doesn't seem to matter much. Hand out fliers, decorate your store, sell snacks, and guess what? You'll still be doing the same couple hundred dollars a day in sales.
4) Customers are dumb, and will wait forever in line (the whole day).
5) You can decorate your store, sort the movies perfectly, whatever you want, but nothing will change. The NPC's will flood in, grab any movies, and check out. At the end of the day the same few hundred will come in.

Best of all - only 2 employees because they can only do two jobs in the entire store! No stocking, no deliveries, no cleaning up/organizing, NOTHING. Just return counter and checkout. This is the weakest shop game I've ever seen regarding employees and management!

This game does the environment/immersion well,  a proper economic system is completely absent from this game. It's flimsy as heck when you get past the nostalgia, decent graphics and immersion. There isn't anything underneath.

I can't believe the developer would do all of this great stuff, but then leave a lot of the systems/processes totally under developed. What the heck?

This game surprised me with how much fun it turned out to be. I like the chill but grindy gameplay. The grinding part of this game is well balanced as to not seem overly tedious and there are a lot of cool unlockables to keep working towards. Being able to hire employees down the road helps as you can focus more on the big picture of running the store but still with a fun mix of day to day activities. I like being able to customize the stores layout with shelving and other items but it has a fairly robust interior design element as well. It's almost "The Sims" like in how easy it is to change wall paper types, flooring, and signage. I also like the aspect of collectable VHS tapes with holographic covers and some of the titles of movies are hilarious and an obvious throwback to 90's movies. If you lived through that era you'll easily recognize the spin offs of the real movies. 

My only two gripes are that it's sometimes difficult to interact with a customer if your standing next to your employee. Several times I've had to go all the way around the counter to be able to interact with the customer because it tries to default you to interacting with the employee. My other gripe is not being able to give employees orders while holding VHS tapes. You have to put ALL the tapes down if you wish to make a quick adjustment with them when you should just be able to verbally tell them. Both of these are mildly annoying and shouldn't affect your purchase decision as they will probably be fixed in future updates

review_text:
A Little Time Machine Disguised as a Game

I absolutely love Retro Rewind.

Being in my 30s, this game hits a very specific nostalgic nerve. It reminds me of being a kid when watching a movie wasn't just opening Netflix and spending 45 minutes scrolling through things you'll never actually watch.

You actually had to go and rent one.

Walking around the store, staring at all the VHS/DVD covers, picking them up because the artwork looked cool, trying to convince whoever you were with that *this* was definitely the film to get... there was something genuinely exciting about it.

Retro Rewind manages to capture that feeling beautifully.

There's something strangely comforting about the whole experience. The aesthetic, the atmosphere and the simple act of browsing movies takes me straight back to childhood. It's not nostalgia that feels forced either. It genuinely reminds me of a time when getting a movie for the evening felt like an event.

And now I'm playing a game that lets me relive it.

Which is slightly horrifying, because apparently I've reached the age where mundane activities from my childhood have become nostalgic historical experiences.

Fantastic.

For anyone who grew up during the video rental era, Retro Rewind feels like a little interactive time capsule. It's cosy, charming and wonderfully familiar.

Sometimes you don't need an enormous open world, a complicated combat system or seventeen different skill trees.

Sometimes you just want to rent a movie again.

review_text:
Overall I love this game. My only criticisms are definitely about subjective things but I'm going to put them here so if you're like me you have the information before you commit to a purchase. 

My first main issue is that there is no incentive at all to decorate and if you, like me, always leave that step to the end rather than a little at a time as you progress you might find yourself not bothering at all. You progress to a point where your income caps out per day (not literally at a definitive amount, but just where you are no longer getting larger and larger profits all the time and you plateau) so after purchasing all of the expansions and getting a decent sized collection of videos that you never run out of any category during the day there aren't any real ways to increase income. Which means after getting all of the achievements already you just kind of have to hang around for a while just to purchase the decorations that have no effects (as far as I can tell). Normally I love decorating in games but in this one it feels pointless as the moment I finish I will never be playing it again.

My second issue is the sheer amount of titles that exist for no reason at all. It is such a vastly overwhelming number and you could not possibly collect them all as there is no infinite storage anywhere (that I've found) and they would definitely not all fit on the shop floor. I like completing collections so that part of my brain could never get itched unfortunately. After you have 1000 titles that is the collecting achievements complete.

The progression is fun and decently paced, I love the character designs, and the gameplay is easy to grasp. It was definitely a fun time I just would like buying a new store section to be locked behind both the cost and maybe having to place 5 decorations each time or something. Or some sort of achievement tied to decorating and more tied to collections with the number of total videos VASTLY reduced. 

A minor issue I has was the run/sprint button only working half of the time.

It sounds like I'm full of complaints but I do genuinely love the overall game, and recommend it as long as the issues above aren't deal breakers for you!

It seems like the perfect game to enjoy with a friend after playing a tough game in the first half.

review_text:
Machine Party is basically what happens when Mario Party gets locked in a basement, handed industrial machinery, and told that friendship is optional.

The minigames are simple enough to understand quickly, but the real fun comes from the panic, betrayal, terrible decisions, and watching your friends meet increasingly unfortunate mechanical endings. The dark industrial atmosphere works surprisingly well with the party-game format, and the physics make every round just unpredictable enough to stay funny.

It’s definitely better with friends. Preferably friends you don’t mind losing.

Pros: chaotic, funny, easy to jump into, great for 2–4 players.
Cons: may cause shouting, revenge, and suspiciously long arguments about “accidental” murder.

Recommended if you enjoy party games but think they could use about 300% more OSHA violations.

review_text:
Presentation is amazing, I'll give this game that.
However, I'd say gameplay would only be fun for 1-2 evenings. 99% of all mini-games have zero variety, so they always play the same (with some of them, this will automatically make you win/lose depending on your minigame knowledge). Some of the mini-games are just unfair and can only be won by pure luck.
Not to mention how stiff and awkward the controls are. Most of the time, once you start doing something, you're locked into an animation until you finish it, and there is a slight (but noticeable) delay before you can do something else.

Those issues are not enough to "ruin" the game, per se, but they do sour the overall experience. I enjoyed my time, with this game, however short it was, but, unless the game receives some QOL and variety updates, I think I've had my fill.
Especially considering that currently the game is literally unplayable if you don't have any friends to play with. There's no solo more or matchmaking.

If you need a fun game to play with friends, just play Buckshot Roulette instead.

review_text:
Machine Party is basically what happens when Mario Party gets locked in a basement, handed industrial machinery, and told that friendship is optional.

The minigames are simple enough to understand quickly, but the real fun comes from the panic, betrayal, terrible decisions, and watching your friends meet increasingly unfortunate mechanical endings. The dark industrial atmosphere works surprisingly well with the party-game format, and the physics make every round just unpredictable enough to stay funny.

It’s definitely better with friends. Preferably friends you don’t mind losing.

Pros: chaotic, funny, easy to jump into, great for 2–4 players.
Cons: may cause shouting, revenge, and suspiciously long arguments about “accidental” murder.

Recommended if you enjoy party games but think they could use about 300% more OSHA violations.

review_text:
I put this somewhere between Saw and Mario Party. Hilariously simplistic shapes and movements paired with gore and an unnerving, dingy ambiance makes this party game stand out. While there's a game mode for everyone's strengths, replayability is limited to 1-2 playthroughs at a time. We play the original mode only to introduce someone to the game. The real fun is in the ability to make playlists and customize rounds, so we can remove stages that we weren't crazy about.
To emerge victorious, you must have the most points. To have the most points, you must win rounds. The way points are racked up should be more obvious. I'd love to see post-game statistics before proceeding to the next stage instead of a random binary visual.
Duck Hunt is a favorite, but we all wished that the obstacles could be randomly generated or change maps to keep it fresh. Spine Breaker and Inside Job may benefit from this as well. On Debris Platforms, there's so much happening so quickly, 3 pieces of junk feels too quick to kill you. A Workshop mode to tweak each stage would be interesting. And we want an online mode!
Being a little nefarious and whimsical makes this friendslop irresistably sloppy. Woohoo! I like this game!!

I had a good laugh with my friends playing this game, but to be honest, I can't recommend it.
It has 15 minigames lasting 2–3 minutes each, and only 5 of them are fun to play. It also has some quality-of-life issues, like not being able to leave the lobby once you select a session type. In minigames where you can push other players, you can just spam the push button in front of someone to prevent them from playing at all. While that might be funny for the person smashing the button, it definitly isn't fun for the player getting pushed.
Overall, I think it's a game with a lot of room for improvement and too little content to play for more than 2 hours at most. I've played other multiplayer games at the same price point that are more fun, much more polished, and packed with way more content.

review_text:
While I would love to recommend the game because it truly is fun and funny, it currently just isn't replayable enough. One run will likely take you about an hour to go through as it cycles through all (i think 15?) minigames. Each one is pretty fun in its own regard, but it just loses that freshness after you play it. This game needs about another 15 minigames and to lower the amount played through each run to help with longevity. The only procedurally generated game is the one where you need to find the syringe as it can be in any searchable cabinet.

Summary:
1. The game only has about 15 minigames with about 13 or 14 of them not being procedurally generated greatly limiting replayability.
2. The game makes you play every single game instead of picking 8-10 max per session randomly(outside of custom lobbies)
3. It needs more minigames (the price for the game is great, but the novelty just dies within an hour or two)

review_text:
[h1]A Great Party Game Full of Chaos[/h1]
Pummel Party is one of those games that's at its best when you have a group of people to play with. The concept is simple enough: compete across different mini-games, collect items, move around the board and do whatever you can to get ahead. But the combination of all these things makes for some genuinely funny and memorable moments.

There's a good variety of mini-games, and most of them are easy to understand without needing much time to learn the rules. Some are more skill-based, while others rely a bit more on luck and timing, which keeps things unpredictable. The board game between the mini-games is just as important, with different items, events and opportunities to mess with the other players. A good lead can disappear pretty quickly when someone gets the right item at the right time.

It's a shame that the developers, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/search/?developer=Rebuilt%20Games]Rebuilt Games[/url], aren't adding more content to the game. I'd love to see new boards, mini-games, items or other ways to keep things fresh. Despite that, I don't feel like the game is unfinished. There's already a solid amount of content here and it feels like a complete package rather than a game that was abandoned halfway through development.

If you enjoy party games and have a group to play with, Pummel Party is definitely worth checking out. It's easy to pick up, has enough variety to keep things interesting and can lead to some absolutely ridiculous games.
